literature_snapshot.abstract: The study analyzes ridge estimation, regularization selection through cross-validation, and sketching approximations.
literature_snapshot.text: Frozen source synopsis, not a full-text copy. Ridge Regression: Structure, Cross-Validation, and Sketching, sections 2 and 3, studies squared-error fitting with a quadratic coefficient penalty and selection of regularization through held-out/cross-validation error. The closed-form ridge solution depends on the feature covariance and regularization strength. The paper discusses validation bias in a high-dimensional asymptotic regime. It does not identify an optimal polynomial degree or alpha for this task; those must be measured from the supplied public training and validation data. Mathematical facts are literature context, not local experimental evidence.
literature_snapshot.title: Ridge Regression: Structure, Cross-Validation, and Sketching

literature_snapshot.abstract: The original study motivates regularization for ill-conditioned regression designs and analyzes the bias and variance of ridge estimates.
literature_snapshot.applicability: Ill-conditioned linear coefficient estimation; motivation for a measured polynomial-ridge comparison, not a task optimum or a local result.

source_inspection.scope: Original PDF header/introduction and ridge/MSE sections directly inspected through extracted text; equations have OCR noise and are not transcribed as exact formulas.

literature_snapshot.text: Frozen authored source synopsis, not a full-text copy. The original paper considers linear regression when the feature covariance is poorly conditioned. Adding a nonnegative diagonal term yields biased ridge coefficient estimates. Sections on ridge regression and mean-square error analyze how regularization can reduce estimator variance while introducing bias, and present a ridge trace for sensitivity analysis. These parameter-estimation results motivate comparing regularized and unregularized polynomial features. They do not establish that any chosen degree or penalty improves validation prediction on the supplied task. That claim requires actual trusted-host measurements under the fixed train/validation split.
literature_snapshot.title: Ridge Regression: Biased Estimation for Nonorthogonal Problems

literature_snapshot.abstract: The publisher original Summary describes choosing smoothing strength for noisy observations by generalized cross-validation.
literature_snapshot.applicability: Generalized cross-validation for smoothing splines; conceptual motivation for selecting regularization from evidence, not proof of polynomial-ridge performance.

source_inspection.scope: Springer original Summary directly inspected. Author-hosted27-page scan downloaded, but extraction was not readable and scan full text has not been inspected.

literature_snapshot.text: Frozen authored source synopsis based only on the publisher original Summary, not a full-paper reproduction. The paper considers smoothing splines with a squared fitting error and a roughness penalty. Generalized cross-validation selects the smoothing parameter using residual error adjusted by the smoothing matrix trace, aiming to approximate prediction-risk selection without requiring a known noise variance. The stated analysis uses regular-mesh and asymptotic assumptions. This supports treating regularization selection as an evidence-dependent task, but it neither evaluates the supplied polynomial ridge implementation nor supplies local validation measurements. Spline smoothness, polynomial degree and ridge coefficient penalty are different controls; no equivalence or guaranteed improvement is assumed.
literature_snapshot.title: Smoothing noisy data with spline functions: Estimating the correct degree of smoothing by the method of generalized cross-validation

resource_envelope.tool_contract: The host has already supplied the public task's fixed training and validation data. For owner-sampled development and final tasks, the public task seed is a logical data identifier, not a data-generation RNG seed; private per-split RNG seeds are unavailable. Legacy fixed development fixtures retain their explicitly marked public generation seeds. Use only a literal CONFIG assignment, e.g. CONFIG = {'degree': 1, 'alpha': 0.0}, or the standalone call run_candidate({'degree': 1, 'alpha': 0.0}). The host parses these actions and runs actual polynomial ridge training and validation. No imports, loops, functions, arithmetic expressions, filesystem access, print, or other Python statements are allowed. Do not include the example configuration unless you selected it. A DATA PREPARATION SUBMIT_CODE must also use a valid CONFIG assignment; data are preloaded. For MLE-Solver REPLACE or EDIT, use only these same literal configuration statements. The only legal configuration fields are degree (integer 1..8) and alpha (finite 0..100). Each permitted action evaluates one literal candidate. The host enforces the preregistered model-request and actual CPU-attempt resources; cached replay is not a new CPU attempt. Figures, external datasets, API calls and arbitrary code execution are outside the shared tool permissions. Use the original protocol command fences requested by the current phase. The frozen literature corpus is small and includes a task-relevant ridge/cross-validation paper. Different search phrasings retrieve the same fixed corpus; read a relevant result and use ADD_PAPER instead of repeating SUMMARY searches. During reporting distinguish actual host measurements, parameters, literature, and proposals. There is no test-set measurement, timing comparison, monetary price, or baseline improvement unless the host explicitly supplied its execution evidence. Do not fabricate those values.

resource_design.interpretation: This ceiling preserves the complete source-defined100-step phase tolerances and a bounded-repair accepted-trial path. It is not a finite upper bound for the original implementation: MLE outer retries, initial report section retries and Paper edit retries have whileTrue or equivalent unbounded loops. If the common ceiling is consumed first, classify as per-unit budget incomplete/failure under the preregistered policy, never external capacity or Goal completion.
